title: Prime a pitcher pump before pumping: pour the priming cup onto the dry leather, then stroke the handle until water flows
instruction: Get the pump going and pump water into the pail.
context: Farmworkers, groundskeepers and camp and park caretakers start hand-operated pitcher pumps on wells, cisterns and garden plots (O*NET 45-2093.00, Farmworkers, Farm, Ranch, and Aquacultural Animals; 37-3011.00, Landscaping and Groundskeeping Workers). A pump that has stood unused loses its prime: the leather plunger cup dries out and shrinks, so stroking the handle only moves air. The start-up is to pour a cup of priming water into the open top of the pump head, onto the leather, so it soaks and seals against the bore, and then stroke the handle steadily until water runs from the spout. Pumping dry first scuffs the dry leather against the cast-iron bore and lifts nothing, pouring too little leaves the cup unsealed, and stopping after a few strokes quits before the water has come up the drop pipe. The priming cup is set back down afterwards and the handle is left at rest.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, x forward, y to the robot's left, table top z = 0. The scene is 0.55 of real size, so volumes are 1:6. A fixed pitcher pump stands on a wooden well platform (10 x 10 x 2.5 cm, centered at (31.5, 0)). The pump head is red-painted cast iron: a base flange 8.4 cm across and 0.8 cm tall on the platform, then a body 6.4 cm across up to its rim at z 9 cm, with a slight flare at the top. The top is open: a bore 5.6 cm across, centered at (32, 0), with the brown leather plunger cup and its nut 4 cm below the rim (z 5 cm). The bore holds 98 mL above the leather; it starts dry. A spout (iron pipe 1.6 cm across) leaves the head's front (+x) at z 7.2 cm and turns down 9 cm out from the axis. The handle is an iron bar (1.2 x 1 cm) with a wooden grip (3.6 x 2.2 x 2 cm, its middle 12 cm from the pivot) on a fulcrum bracket at the head's left side (+y), pivot at (32, 3.6, 11.5), reaching out toward +y; it swings about the x axis between 20 degrees up (its rest: the plunger rod's weight holds it there) and 25 degrees down, so the top of the grip travels from z 16.6 to 7.3 cm. A fixed steel pail (9 cm across, 5.2 cm tall, 8.4 cm inside, holding 271 mL) stands under the spout, centered at (41.7, 0). A free white enamel cup with a blue rim (4 cm across, 7.5 cm tall, 3.5 cm inside, 40 g) stands at (25, -8) holding 40 mL of water (240 mL real, one cup), shown blue.
scoring: Definitions: a stroke is the handle going from at least 12 degrees up to at least 15 degrees down (60 % of its 45-degree swing). The leather seals while at least 20 mL stands on it in the head (8 mm of water over its 6 mm flared lip; 120 mL real). A stroke while it seals is wet; the first 3 wet strokes draw the air out of the drop pipe and every later one delivers 75 mL (450 mL real) from the spout into the pail. A stroke before the head holds 20 mL is dry; one or two while the priming water goes in are common practice and barely touch the leather, but more than two scuffs the dry leather, which is never undone. At the end, let go means no gripper holding the cup (fingers under 60 % open within 4.5 cm of it), no tool point within 4 cm of the handle's grip, and the handle back up past 12 degrees. Scores: no pumped water in the pail (doing nothing, pumping unprimed or with too little priming water, stopping within 3 wet strokes, or pouring the priming water into the pail), or anything still held at the end: 0. Pumped water in the pail but more than two dry strokes first: 0.25. Under 150 mL pumped (two delivering strokes, 0.9 L real): 0.5. 150 mL or more but the cup not standing upright (within 10 degrees), still, on the table outside the pail: 0.75. All of it with both arms home and still: 1.0; an arm not home: 0.9. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9, 1.0. In a real trial, count from the video the strokes made before the priming water was in, measure the priming water poured with a marked cup and the pail's water with a measuring jug, and check the cup and handle at the end.
reset_notes: Open the pump's drain (or lift the plunger and sponge the bore) so the head is empty and the pump has lost its prime, and swap in a dry leather cup from a set kept on hand, since a damp one still seals. Empty the pail, refill the cup with 240 mL (40 mL in the sim) and stand it on its mark, and let the handle rest up against its top stop.
fidelity: The scene is 0.55 of real size, so volumes are 1:6. No fluid or air is simulated: the priming water is a flow model that pours from the tipped cup straight down into the open head, and the pump is a stroke-counting model in which the leather seals with 20 mL on it, 3 strokes lift the water and each stroke after that adds 75 mL to the pail. Leather wear is not modeled beyond the dry-stroke rule, and the handle's return is a spring for the plunger rod's weight.
